D.t: Jamie Davis trails by 6.5 and wins 16% of simulations. Closing it takes about 49,687 voters switching sides, or 99,374 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +14.4 and D +1.8. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +2.2. Your best recent poll is Hart Research Associates (D) at R +1.8; your worst is Hart Research Associates (D) at R +5.9. 2 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Orleans Parish, a projected net 104,070 votes; East Baton Rouge Parish, a projected net 43,798 votes; Caddo Parish, a projected net 14,368 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.

The large counties within 12 points: Jefferson Parish, D +2.2, 8.9% of the vote; St. Landry Parish, D +0.5, 1.8% of the vote; St. Mary Parish, R +11.8, 1.0% of the vote; St. Bernard Parish, R +9.7, 0.8% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jamie Davis runs furthest behind in Livingston Parish, Bossier Parish, Ouachita Parish. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters without a degree, 68% of voters, 46 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.40 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 46 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.29 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 61% of voters, 50 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.05 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Jamie Davis: Immigration voters 15 to 85, White voters 34 to 66, Midsize counties 39 to 61. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$479K cash against $1.4M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.4 points away from Jamie Davis. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
